_comment: The specialised task. Everything after section 02 reads this file instead of hard-coding a dataset (SPEC §4). Provisional pick from reports/bakeoff.md (issue #1): HRF retina vessels as native-resolution 1024 px crops. Simone may swap it for DSB2018 nuclei; then change this file and re-run scripts/prepare_data.py and scripts/precompute.py.
name: HRF retina vessels
long_name: HRF (High-Resolution Fundus) retinal vessel segmentation, native-resolution 1024 px crops
citation: Budai A, Bock R, Maier A, Hornegger J, Michelson G. Robust Vessel Segmentation in Fundus Images. International Journal of Biomedical Imaging, 2013.
hook: Annotating the vessels of one fundus image by hand takes roughly 3 to 5 hours (FIVES paper, Jin et al. 2022).

preprocessing.note: One random 1024x1024 crop per image inside the field of view with >= 5 % vessel pixels (vessels 4-20 px wide). The whole fundus downsampled to 1024 px long side is kept as 'full' for the section 02 failure gallery (vessels 1-3 px wide there).

scribble_generator.note: Foreground strokes = ground-truth skeleton segments (cut at junctions) with 70 % of the segments dropped (SPEC §4). Background strokes = random polylines that stay away from the vessels.

missing_labels.note: Hide ~50 % of the vessel segments; the hidden pixels keep their true label only in the evaluation mask.

gradcam.note: Every image contains vessels, so there is no image-level negative class. The bake-off calls the patch-level proxy an awkward fit; say so in section 06.
